etymology: Latin: argumentum ad naturam - the natural is treated as the good, as though the word carried a verdict.
committed_when: A product, practice, or hierarchy needs a justification.
tell: The justification is a claim about what is natural, with no account of why natural is good.
counter: Ask which part of nature is the model. Nature also contains arsenic, parasites, and every hierarchy that ever existed.
senses: Concluding that something is right or healthy because it is natural, or wrong because it is artificial.
It works because "natural" smuggles in a standard it never defends. Nature is a description; the sentence spends it as an endorsement.
example: *"It is natural for people to sort themselves by tribe."* It is also natural to die of an infected cut, and we stopped doing that on purpose.

confused_with.tell: Tradition cites age, nature cites origin; both answer a question about value with a question about ancestry.
